MassiveID.description: The unique identifier for the dataset in the MassIVE repository.

filename.description: The name of the spectral mz(X)ML file with extension. The filename should be unique within the dataset. Contact us if you are not able to provide this file format.

SampleType.description: Vague descriptor of analyzed sample type. Make especially sure you label blanks correctly.

SampleTypeSub1.description: Further descriptor of analyzed sample type. Make especially sure you label blanks correctly.

ProductCategory.description: The category of a personal care product (SampleType personal care product; also household products such as dish washing liquid): the most specific category of the personalCareProductMASST product tree (e.g. 'Sunscreen' for Personal Care > Cosmetics > Skin Care > Sunscreen). Free text.

FoodOntologyTerm.description: The food or beverage sampled, as a term of the Global FoodOmics food ontology (GFOP) used by foodMASST, at the most specific level known (a food, e.g. hazelnut, or a food group, e.g. nut). Mixed dishes ('complex') have no term. You can find all allowed terms in the resource link.
FoodOntologyTerm.source: GFOP (Global FoodOmics food ontology, WebProtégé) as used by foodMASST: https://github.com/robinschmid/microbe_masst/blob/master/data/food_masst_tree.json (labels, IDs and paths: bin/translation_sheets/GFOP_food_ontology.csv)

NCBITaxonomy.description: Enter a Taxonomy ID and NCBI name separated by |. ***if multiple organisms are present in a sample - please separate different entries by || (e.g. 562|Escherichia coli||29387|Staphylococcus sp.)

YearOfAnalysis.description: The year the sample was analyzed.

SampleCollectionMethod.description: The method used to collect the sample.
allowed_values: solid material, dried in silica at room temperature
solid material, PDMS patch, head space solid phase microextraction
solid material, head space solid phase microextraction
in vivo, head space solid phase microextraction

SampleExtractionMethod.description: The method used to extract the sample.

InternalStandardsUsed.description: The internal standards used in the analysis, as names of this list (the GNPS template names and the names public sources state; a new name is added here, not accepted as free text). Several standards are joined by ';' (new combinations in alphabetical order); 'none' means no internal standard was used.

MassSpectrometer.description: The mass spectrometer used in the analysis. We rely on an ontobee publicly controlled vocabulary for this field. Provide the name and the MS_ID of the mass spectrometer separated by |.

IonizationSourceAndPolarity.description: The ionization source and polarity used in the analysis.

ChromatographyAndPhase.description: The chromatography and phase used in the analysis.

SubjectIdentifierAsRecorded.description: Provide an identifier for sampled individuals. If the same subject (e.g. person, or mouse) is sampled multiple times, the same identifier should be used for all samples from that subject. Any text or number can be used as an identifier. Make sure to remove any personal information from the identifier!

AgeInYears.description: The age of the subject in years. If you have ages in another unit such as days please convert to years.

BiologicalSex.description: The biological sex of the subject. Where none is recorded, a mammal sample of a body part only one sex has (UBERON/CL, e.g. cervical mucus, testis; milk unless the subject is a child) gives it.

UBERONBodyPartName.description: The name of the body part sampled. While the column is called UBERONBodyPartName we also support the Cell ontology and Plant ontology in this field. You can find all allowed terms in the resource links.
UBERONBodyPartName.source:
Animal bodyparts: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/uberon 
Cell types: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/cl 
Plant parts: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/po

TermsofPosition.description: The position of the body part sampled such as left or right arm.

HealthStatus.description: The health status of the subject.

SmokingStatus.description: The tobacco smoking status of the subject at the time of sampling. 'non-smoker' is used when the source only states that the subject does not currently smoke, without saying whether they never or formerly smoked.

BodyMassIndex.description: The body mass index (BMI) of the subject in kg/m^2. Values outside 10-60 (implausible extremes, e.g. auto-miscalculated BMIs) are rejected as missing.

Diet.description: What the subject ate: its dietary regimen (an experimental or composition diet, or a human dietary pattern; terms aligned with the Ontology for Nutritional Studies (ONS), e.g. high-fat diet) or, when the dietary treatment is a food the subject ate or was fed (e.g. in the feed or drinking water), that food as a GFOP term. The food terms are those of FoodOntologyTerm (without its general classes such as plant or animal, and water), added to these allowed values when the workflow runs; FoodOntologyTerm itself describes samples that are foods. One value per sample: a regimen other than the control diet wins over a food given with it (the food then stays in SampleGroupFreeText). Only for samples of animals (NCBITaxonomy in Metazoa, humans included) that are not themselves foods, blanks, QCs, standards, cultures or cell lines.
Diet.source: ONS (regimen terms); GFOP (Global FoodOmics food ontology) as used by foodMASST for foods, the same terms as FoodOntologyTerm (bin/translation_sheets/GFOP_food_ontology.csv)

DOIDCommonName.description: The common name of the disease or condition of the subject. You can find all allowed terms in the resource link.

ComorbidityListDOIDIndex.description: DOID IDs of comorbidities, in any number and combination. Please separate multiple comorbidities by a |. Every listed ID must be a current (not obsolete) DOID ID; you can find all IDs in the resource link.

HPOCommonName.description: A health condition or phenotype of the subject that is not a disease, e.g. sepsis, cachexia or acute kidney injury. Diseases go to DOIDCommonName. Terms are the labels of the 'Phenotypic abnormality' branch of the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO); you can find all allowed terms in the resource link.

Exposure.description: What the subject was exposed to, as an experimental treatment or as an environmental or lifestyle exposure, e.g. exposure to ozone or exposure to particulate matter. Terms are the labels of the Environmental Conditions, Treatments and Exposures Ontology (ECTO); for plants also of the Plant Experimental Conditions Ontology (PECO). You can find all allowed terms in the resource links.

OrganismExposureAgent.description: (automatically generated) What the organism was exposed to, taken from the ECTO term in Exposure ('has exposure stimulus'): a chemical (ChEBI), environmental material (ENVO), organism (NCBITaxon), food (FOODON) or procedure (MAXO). Empty for PECO terms, which do not name an agent.

TimePointHoursRelativeToEvent.description: Time of sampling in hours relative to the study's reference event (e.g. start of treatment, infection or intervention). Negative values are before the event. Only filled from values that state a number with a time unit (1 day = 24 h, 1 week = 168 h, 1 month = 730 h).

FastingStatus.description: Whether the subject was fasted before sampling.

ColonizationStatus.description: The microbial colonization status of the host: germ-free (no microorganisms), gnotobiotic (only known microorganisms, e.g. monocolonized or colonized with a defined consortium), specific-pathogen-free (free of a defined list of pathogens, otherwise a conventional microbiota) or conventional (an undefined, normal microbiota).
ColonizationStatus.source: microbiomeMASST (Charron-Lamoureux et al., bioRxiv 2026, https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.04.703849): colonization status, e.g. germ-free, monocolonized, specific-pathogen free

SampleGroupFreeText.description: The sample's experimental group as defined by the study, in the study's own wording, from grouping factors that no other ReDU column covers (e.g. genotype, intervention arm, cohort). Several grouping factors are separated by ';' as 'Factor: value; Factor: value'. Only filled when the study has at least 2 groups and on average at least 2 samples per group.

CellLine.description: The cell line the sample comes from, as the Cellosaurus recommended name (one cell line per sample). Cellosaurus accessions (CVCL_...) and synonyms of exactly one cell line are converted to the recommended name. You can find all allowed terms in the resource link.

SampleCollectionDateandTime.description: Date (and optionally time) the sample was collected, normalised to precision-preserving ISO-8601 so the temporal resolution is explicit: year (2018), year-month (2018-07), date (2018-07-12) or date+time (2018-07-12T22:00); a collection period is an interval start/end (2022-06-14/2022-06-30). US M/D/Y, ISO Y-M-D, textual months (12 July 2018), 2-digit years and timezone-suffixed values are accepted. Ambiguous slash dates are resolved per dataset (a value proving an order wins; otherwise the dataset decides; default month-first, NORMAN day-first). Only the submitted precision is kept - days or times are never fabricated.

Country.description: The country where the sample was collected.

HumanPopulationDensity.description: The population density of the area where the sample was collected or the sampled individual is from.

LatitudeandLongitude.description: Enter latitude and longitude separated by a |. please convert GPS coordinates using a GPS coordinates converter.

DepthorAltitudeMeters.description: enter depths as negative values from sea-level (e.g. -200 m) and altitudes as positive values from sea-level (e.g. 2000 m)

qiita_sample_name.description: Enter the sample_name of a corresponding sequencing file in Qiita (https://qiita.ucsd.edu/) for cross-platform connectivity. The identifier must be exact and prepended with the Qiita identifier. *Note, files names should be entered as present in Qiita which does not allow for underscores or special characters

UniqueSubjectID.description: (automatically generated) formula which generates massive ID number & SubjectID

LifeStage.description: (automatically generated) The life range of the subject if human.

UBERONOntologyIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the UBERON body part name.

DOIDOntologyIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the DOID common name.

HPOOntologyIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the HPO common name.

ExposureIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the exposure term (ECTO or PECO).

OrganismExposureAgentIndex.description: (automatically generated) The ontology ID of the exposure agent (CHEBI, ENVO, NCBITaxon, FOODON, MAXO, ...).

CellLineIndex.description: (automatically generated) The Cellosaurus accession of the cell line.

FoodOntologyIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the GFOP food ontology term in FoodOntologyTerm: the local ID of its WebProtégé IRI (the IRI is http://webprotege.stanford.edu/<ID>).
FoodOntologyIndex.source: GFOP (Global FoodOmics food ontology, WebProtégé) as used by foodMASST: https://github.com/robinschmid/microbe_masst/blob/master/data/food_masst_tree.json (labels, IDs and paths: bin/translation_sheets/GFOP_food_ontology.csv)

NCBIRank.description: (automatically generated) The rank of the NCBITaxonomy as specified by NCBI.

NCBIDivision.description: (automatically generated) The division of the NCBITaxonomy as specified by NCBI.

ENVOEnvironmentBiome.description: The biome of the environment where the sample was collected. All terms given in the label column of the resource link are allowed.

ENVOEnvironmentMaterial.description: The material of the environment where the sample was collected. All terms given in the label column of the resource link are allowed.

ENVOBroadScale.description: In this field, report which major environmental system your sample or specimen came from. The systems identified should have a coarse spatial grain, to provide the general environmental context of where the sampling was done (e.g. were you in the desert or a rainforest?).

ENVOLocalScale.description: In this field, report the entity or entities which are in your sample or specimen’s local vicinity and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample or specimen.

ENVOMediumScale.description: In this field, report which environmental material or materials (pipe separated) immediately surrounded your sample or specimen prior to sampling.

ENVOEnvironmentBiomeIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the ENVO environment biome.

ENVOEnvironmentMaterialIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the ENVO environment material.

ENVOLocalScaleIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the ENVOLocalScale.

ENVOBroadScaleIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the ENVOBroadScale.

ENVOMediumScaleIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the ENVOMediumScale.

IsolationSourceNCBITaxonomy.description: For an organism cultured from a sample (an isolate, e.g. a bacterium or fungus): the organism it was isolated from, e.g. the plant, sponge or coral. Enter a Taxonomy ID and NCBI name separated by |, as in NCBITaxonomy (the same allowed terms); several organisms are separated by ||. NCBITaxonomy is the organism analyzed (the isolate); Country, LatitudeandLongitude, DepthorAltitudeMeters, SampleCollectionDateandTime and ENVOEnvironmentBiome are where and when it was collected. An organism that is also in NCBITaxonomy is left out.

IsolationSourceUBERONBodyPartName.description: For an isolate: the body part of the organism in IsolationSourceNCBITaxonomy it was isolated from, e.g. leaf or root. The same allowed terms as UBERONBodyPartName (UBERON, Cell Ontology and Plant Ontology), which names the body part analyzed. For a plant, a UBERON term that has the name of a Plant Ontology term becomes that term (cortex: PO:0005708), as in UBERONBodyPartName.
IsolationSourceUBERONBodyPartName.source:
Animal bodyparts: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/uberon 
Cell types: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/cl 
Plant parts: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/po

IsolationSourceUBERONOntologyIndex.description: (automatically generated) The index of the IsolationSourceUBERONBodyPartName.

IsolationSourceENVOEnvironmentMaterial.description: For an isolate: the environmental material it was isolated from, e.g. marine sediment or sea water. The same allowed terms as ENVOEnvironmentMaterial, which names the material analyzed.

IsolationSourceENVOEnvironmentMaterialIn.description: (automatically generated) The index of the IsolationSourceENVOEnvironmentMaterial.

DataSource.description: (automatically generated) Repository the file is hosted at.

USI.description: (automatically generated) The unique identifier of the spectral raw file in the repository. Which can be used to access the file thorugh various tools.
